newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

AFL club Melbourne has named Garry Lyon captain for his 200th game against the Sydney Swans tonight. Lyon is recovering from a calf strain that caused him to miss last week's clash. For Sydney's first home game of the season, Paul Roos and Mark Bayes return from injury, but Andrew Dunkley is absent on suspension. Page 20.

Queensland Tri-Series Super League coach Wayne Bennett has defended his star player Allan Langer's tackling style and accused rival state coach Tim Sheens of club loyalties and gamesmanship. Queensland is favourite for the opening Tri-Series game in Sydny tonight. Page 20.

ACT Brumbies rugby union captain Brett Robinson is frustrated that his side is seen as a second-rate side formed of inter-state players. The Brumbies have started the year well, but also did well last year in the preliminary rounds before missing th semi-finals. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Super League's opening Tri-Series game looks likely to be a financial disaster with as many as 17,000 tickets being given away and no sponsor yet to sign for the series. For the game to break even, about 14,000 fans will have to pay full price, and this is unlikely with as few as 1,900 seats being sold so far. Page 40.

As Octagonal prepares for his last ride at the Queen Elizabeth Stakes at Randwick on Saturday, fans are seeking last-minute memorabilia. Australian Jockey Club marketing man John McGhee has called the week "madness" as unprecedented support for a horse's final race increases. Page 40.

The women's National Basketball League starts tonight, with the Sydney Flames early favourites to win the premiership. There are indications the League will be more even this year, as substantial off-season player movement and the ongoing United States professional leagues have relocated player talent. Page 38.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League reserves competition's present system will remain until at least the end of the 1998 season. Meetings will be held with clubs from next week to discuss alternatives to the reserves competition. Page D3.

The 500cc world motorcycle championship season begins this weekend in Kuala Lumpur. Australia's Michael Doohan is in search of his fourth consecutive world title and has found inspiration from his Honda teammate Alex Criville, who strongly rivals him for status as the leading rider in the championship. Page D10.

Although Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor is to keep playing in the remaining one-day internationals in South Africa, he is being over-ruled by co-selectors Ian Healy and coach Geoff Marsh. Brendon Julian, and not Taylor as expected, is on standby forthe injured Mark Waugh to replace Michael DiVenuto in today's match. Page D13.
THE HERALD SUN

AFL club Carlton will not play in its traditional navy blue strip against Adelaide on Sunday, but in a light blue strip to receive A$250,000 in sponsorship from Mars Confectionary. To promote Mars' new blue M&M chocolates, Carlton will change their colours for one week only. Page 1.

AFL football operations manager Ian Collins does not believe the introduction of an appeals board would stop players challenging tribunal decisions in court. Collins will not remove a player's common law right to appeal, or implement any new systems, aftr Greg Williams' Supreme Court injunction allowed him to play while suspended. Page 100.

The Gippsland Falcons soccer team will boycott their national league cup match tomorrow against Adelaide City if an opposition player wears protective goggles. Adelaide player Angelo Costanzo has had eye surgery and is permitted to play only if wearing protection, but the Falcons will protest because they feel their own players may be hurt if in a heading clash with Costanzo. Page 90.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The New South Wales Waratahs rugby union side will play the strong South African team Free State on Saturday night at the Sydney Football Stadium. If the Waratahs can defeat Free State and Queensland next week, they can still make the semi-finals. Page 13.

ARL side Parramatta will wear light-blue jerseys in their game against Manly tomorrow night for the first time in their 50-year history in a sponsorship deal with the Mars confectionary company to promote a new brand of chocolates. Page 115.

New South Wales Opposition Leader Peter Collins has called for an urgent motion to debate the taxation issue in the State's racing industry. Collins believes the Government should be criticised for failing to deliver taxation relief to the troubled indusry. Page 112.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
